Ganpati idol falls during procession in Mumbai; 2 dead, 5 injured
articles.description: Two individuals died and five others sustained injuries when a large Ganpati idol collapsed during its procession. The idol fell due to an apparent welding issue with its supporting frame, police officials stated. The incident occurred late Saturday night as the procession neared its destination in Bhuleshwar. The deceased included the Ganpati mandal president, Sanket Nevshe. Investigations into the exact circumstances of the accident are currently underway by authorities.

articles.description: The Indian Army has opened registrations for Terrier Cyber Quest 2026, a national competition. This event focuses on cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and digital awareness for participants. The competition features three tracks: Bug Hunting, AI Kavach, and National Creators Challenge. Finalists will receive certificates, medallions, cash prizes, and national recognition for their achievements. Winners may also get opportunities to visit defense establishments and contribute to future initiatives.

articles.title: NTA needs reform, not replacement, says former UGC chairman
articles.description: Former UGC Chairman Mamidala Jagadesh Kumar stated NTA needs structural strengthening. He views exam security as an end-to-end challenge given the scale. He emphasized building permanent professional capacity and dependable examination centers.

articles.title: Four MIT dropouts, all under 27, built Cursor and sold it to SpaceX for $60 billion: How a failed idea became an AI giant
articles.description: Four young MIT dropouts turned a failed early idea into Anysphere, the company behind AI coding tool Cursor. After initially exploring an AI copilot for mechanical engineers, founders Michael Truell, Aman Sanger, Sualeh Asif and Arvid Lunnemark pivoted to AI-powered software development. Cursor rapidly grew into a multibillion-dollar company before SpaceX acquired Anysphere for $60 billion in 2026. The founders’ journey highlights how abandoning an unsuccessful idea and adapting to emerging technology can transform a startup’s fortunes.

articles.title: At 7, he entered Guinness records; at 16, built a satellite: How a 20-year-old from Jammu raised $4.3 million for a space startup
articles.description: Jammu-born entrepreneur Onkar Singh Batra began building technology at seven, wrote a book at 12 and founded a company at 13. At 16, he built InQube, an open-source satellite, which exposed him to communication gaps faced by satellites in low Earth orbit. He later founded Apolink in Silicon Valley to develop an in-space communication network for satellites. At 20, Batra has raised $4.3 million and is working to build continuous connectivity infrastructure for space.
